title: Aquagenic Syringeal Acrokeratoderma Successfully Managed with Topical Glycopyrronium: A Case and Review of the Literature
content: Acquired aquagenic syringeal acrokeratoderma (ASA) is a rare dermatological disorder characterised by transient oedematous papules and palmar wrinkling following water exposure. Multiple treatment modalities have been described, however evidence supporting effective therapies is limited. We report a case of a 21-year-old Indian male with a 2-year history of painful palmar wrinkling, tingling, and stinging occurring approximately 15 minutes after water exposure, with associated pruritus and peeling following prolonged immersion. Clinical findings were consistent with acquired ASA, and investigations excluded systemic disease. Initial treatment with topical 20% aluminium chloride was discontinued because of excessive dryness. Subsequent treatment with topical glycopyrronium bromide 2% spray produced a 50% reduction in symptom severity without adverse effects, with sustained improvement over 1.5 years. This favourable response supports current evidence for a pathogenic role for eccrine gland dysfunction and sweating in ASA and suggests that epithelial transmembrane channelopathy with sweat leakage may contribute to disease development. Treatments targeting these pathways may therefore be effective strategies and topical glycopyrronium bromide can be a therapeutic consideration in ASA. Further studies are needed to validate these mechanisms and establish optimal management strategies.
